READING THE MAP

A starting point for your sounder.

The letters rank mapped rocky habitat for investigation. They do not grade catches, charter popularity, or how safe a spot is to fish.

A

First look 75–100

The strongest overall combination of rocky cover, relief, uneven terrain, and nearby habitat in this atlas. Start your search here when conditions and access suit.

B

Useful alternatives 55–74

Meaningful mapped structure, with a lower combined score in one or more factors. Good options to investigate when another area is crowded or the drift is awkward.

C

Exploratory Below 55

A lower terrain score, often reflecting less relief, less rocky cover, or a smaller nearby patch. A productive isolated feature can still score C.

Score weights: relief 35 points, rough/bedrock cover 30, terrain unevenness 20, nearby rough habitat area 15. A large rocky area alone cannot earn A. These are chosen research weights; they have not been validated against catches. See the scoring method.

Point, shaded area, or dashed line?

Lettered marker: a place to begin a sounder search, not a confirmed individual boulder. Shaded area: a selected footprint of mapped rocky habitat, not the whole reef. Dashed line: an alignment over structure you could try to cross if your measured drift allows; it is not a safe approach route or a current forecast.

Survey depths are referenced to MLLW. The water depth you see depends on the tide. Confirm bottom and depth on your sounder, and use current charts and protected-area boundaries before setting a drift.

A SEPARATE KIND OF EVIDENCE

Historical charter AIS

Know what’s on the map.

This public edition contains 132 habitat candidates, 107 partial reef outlines, and 31 optional drift alignments derived from 2008 USGS surveys. The research screen is dated September 20, 2026.

A = 75–100 (first look), B = 55–74 (useful alternatives), C = below 55 (exploratory). Grades rank measured terrain, not expected catches. There are no verified catches or AIS-confirmed charter hotspots at these coordinates. Outlines show selected habitat; they are not the complete reef. Lines suggest an alignment over structure, not a boat route or a prediction of your drift.

Depths use the survey’s MLLW reference. Tides, position uncertainty, and seabed change affect the depth you find. Confirm depth and structure with your sounder.

Cambria and historical charter annotations are excluded from this public edition while source reuse terms are unresolved. Protected-area boundaries and the Diablo Canyon security zone are not displayed as a live layer. A marker does not establish current legal access.
